title: Returned-Payment Block Settings for Placed Consumer Accounts
content:
Payments risk table for **Placed Consumer Accounts**. It sets, per placement stage, how many returned payments trigger a block of the electronic payment channels, the rolling window over which returned payments are counted, and how long the block lasts.

| Stage | Returned payments that trigger the block | Counting window (rolling calendar days) | Block length (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Early-Out Placement | 2 | 180 | 60 |
| Primary Placement | 2 | 180 | 90 |
| Secondary Placement | 2 | 180 | 90 |
| Tertiary Placement | 2 | 180 | 120 |
| Warehouse Placement | 2 | 180 | 120 |
| Legal Review Placement | 1 | 180 | 180 |

## Column definitions

- **Returned payments that trigger the block**: the number of returned payments within the counting window that triggers a block of the electronic payment channels on the account.
- **Counting window**: the rolling window, in calendar days, over which returned payments are counted.
- **Block length**: the calendar days the electronic payment channels stay blocked after the block is triggered.

## Reading the table

- The counting window is 180 days at every stage.
- Legal Review Placement is the only stage where a single returned payment is enough; every other stage needs two.
- Block lengths rise with the stage: 60 days at Early-Out Placement, 90 at Primary Placement and Secondary Placement, 120 at Tertiary Placement and Warehouse Placement, and 180 at Legal Review Placement.

*Hypothetical comparison:* an account with exactly one returned payment inside the window meets the trigger at Legal Review Placement and does not meet it at Primary Placement.
